newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-ZIMBABWE AND INDIA TIE IN FRANTIC FINISH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ZIMBABWE AND INDIA TIE IN FRANTIC FINISH.

text.p: India and Zimbabwe tied their triangular series match in bizarre fashion on Monday when late order batsman Robin Singh was run out off the final ball of the match which was signalled a wide.
India needed two runs from the final delivery from Eddo Brandes with the last pair at the wicket and Robin Singh, on 48 not out, on strike.

Brandes delivered the ball down the legside and although Singh was run out at the bowler's end, umpire Rudi Koertzen was already signalling the wide that made the scores level and ensured both sides took one point from a tie.

Wicketkeeper Andy Flower and Brandes combined to effect the run out. If Singh had stood his ground he would have had an extra ball from which to hit the single needed to win the match. It left India all out for 236 in reply to Zimbabwe's 236 for eight.

India had looked out of the hunt as Brandes, who finished with figures of five for 41, dismissed Sachin Tendulkar and Mohammad Azharuddin for six apiece in an opening burst of three for 20 from six overs.

India's 40 for three became 110 for five but all the middle order chipped in to keep the target in range. Rahul Dravid made 23, Saba Karim 38 and Ajay Jadeja 32 to keep their side in touch before Singh's innings proved vital.

He made his runs from only 32 balls, including a straight six off a Heath Streak no ball in the penultimate over to bring the asking rate down from 27 off the last two overs and then 11 from the last six balls.
Zimbabwe's impressive 236 for eight on a slow pitch was founded on a 94-run fourth-wicket partnership between captain Alistair Campbell (61) and Strang (47).
They revived the innings after Zimbabwe had stuttered to 51 for three but it was a brutal 40 in 32 balls, including three sixes, from all-rounder Craig Evans which carried Zimbabwe well beyond 200.
Zimbabwe and India each have one point from two matches while South Africa have won both their matches to top the table.
Zimbabwe meet South Africa in the next match in Cape Town on Wednesday.
